subject: Annual wallet maturity schedule & staged commitment proposal
messages:
From: Anna Li <anna@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Intro — multi-year prepay idea for inference usage

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Nimbus is trying to lock a long-term inference budget for a set of customer-facing features we expect to scale in 2027. We want a structure that balances our cash planning with predictable unit economics — thinking about a multi-year prepay with an annual top-up and a monthly drawdown (wallet) so we can smooth usage spikes.

Attached is a short one-pager on expected usage and a rough calendarized burn profile for year 1. Broad asks:
- Can Redwood offer term discounts for a 3-year commitment?
- Can we structure a prepay wallet that decrements monthly against real usage, with unused months rolling into the next year?
- Any protections if our usage is materially below forecast in year 1?

Procurement (procurement@nimbusanalytics.com) is on copy. Happy to hop on a call to walk through numbers.

Thanks,
Anna
Director, Cloud & ML Ops
Nimbus Analytics

[attachment: Nimbus_Payg_Usage_1pager.pdf (pdf)]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@nimbusanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-16T09:48:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Intro — multi-year prepay idea for inference usage

Anna — great to hear, and this is exactly the sort of predictability we design for. High-level thoughts below; I can put a formal proposal together after a quick follow-up call.

Proposal (outline):
- Term: 3 years with annual tops (client prepays an agreed annual wallet amount at the start of each contract year).
- Drawdown: Monthly wallet decrement based on actual usage (tokens/embedding units). If a month is under forecast, the leftover credits stay in the wallet and can be consumed later in the contract year; at year boundary we offer a rollover up to 10% of that year’s wallet into next year or a credit at negotiated rate.
- Discounts: Tiered term discount on committed prepay: Year 1 baseline (no term discount beyond volume tiers), Year 2: +X% term discount, Year 3: +Y% (we'll propose exact %s based on commitment).
- True-up: Quarterly true-up against actuals with monthly invoicing for overages or crediting for under-usage.
- Safeguard: If usage is < 60% of forecast in Year 1, a remediation path that includes an option to convert remaining wallet to a reduced-rate carry-forward plus a modest credit to Nimbus (avoid full refunds).

Questions for you before I draft the SOW:
1) Do you prefer an annual fixed dollar top-up or a MW/committed token quantity?
2) Are you ok with a 10% cap on rollovers, or do you want an alternative (e.g., full rollover with a renewal true-up)?

I’m looping in Marissa and Karthik for pricing and legal touchpoints. If procurement wants a sample SOW and a model, I’ll attach both.

- Evelyn
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: internal: initial math and an example amortization profile

Eve / Karthik — quick internal note with a concrete example to attach to the customer SOW. I threw together a simple amortization and sensitivity in the attached spreadsheet. Key levers: upfront prepay amount, annual top-up cadence, rollover cap, and discount schedule.

Example (numbers illustrative):
- Year 1 prepay: $1.2M (expected monthly burn average $100k)
- Year 2 top-up: $1.0M
- Year 3 top-up: $900k
- Discount schedule on committed wallet: Year1 = 8% off list for committed volume bands (>= $1M), Year2 = 12%, Year3 = 16% (scale can be renegotiated by band).
- Rollover: up to 10% of unused wallet per year; beyond that, unused amounts convert to a 6-month limited credit at 70% of list.

Risk items: if they spike massively in a single month, our batching benefits may degrade — propose a per-request concurrency cap clause and an agreed surge capacity pricing (e.g., usage above 3x monthly baseline billed at on-demand + 25%).

Attaching: prepay_model_20261117.xlsx (contains per-month token forecasts and three sensitivity scenarios).

-Marissa
Senior Pricing Manager

[attachment: prepay_model_20261117.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: internal: initial math and an example amortization profile

Agree with Marissa's model. A couple of contract-level clauses to protect Redwood while keeping Nimbus comfortable:
- Quarterly true-up with a 30-day invoice cycle for any overage.
- Early termination: if Nimbus terminates for convenience in Year 1, unused wallet converts to a pro-rata credit less a 10% administrative fee; Years 2–3 have a lower fee (5%).
- Rollover cap: 10% as proposed, with an explicit carve-out allowing one full-year rollover once during the term if they provide 60 days’ notice and a revised forecast.

For discounts, recommend we propose: Year1 = 10%, Year2 = 15%, Year3 = 20% on the committed wallet (these are headline term discounts; final effective discount will still depend on volume banding).

I’ll mark DEAL-8931 in our pipeline and run legal to draft the redline. Ben — tagging you for any final commercial concessions.

- Karthik
Director, Deal Structuring

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
To: Anna Li <anna@nimbusanalytics.com>, procurement@nimbusanalytics.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-22T10:02:00-08:00
Subject: Proposal: 3-year staged prepay wallet (formal SOW attached)

Anna / procurement — attaching a formal SOW and the pricing model for Nimbus (see attachments). Summary of the proposed commercial terms:
- Structure: 3-year agreement with annual prepay top-ups. Wallet decrements monthly based on actual usage.
- Commit / Discount: Headline term discounts applied to the committed wallet: Yr1 = 10%, Yr2 = 15%, Yr3 = 20%. Volume banding will be applied to compute final per-unit pricing in the SOW.
- Rollover & True-up: Up to 10% rollover per year; quarterly true-ups; monthly billing for overages.
- Early termination & remediation: Year1 termination fee 10% of unused wallet; Year2–3 = 5% fee. One-time full-year rollover allowed with 60 days’ notice.
- Surge: Agreed surge pricing (on-demand + 25%) above 3x monthly baseline to protect capacity.

Requested next steps:
1) Please confirm if you prefer dollar-denominated top-ups or token-unit top-ups.
2) If acceptable, we’ll send a DocuSign for signature and include the SOW + model.
3) If procurement wants a tighter rollover or a different true-up cadence, flag it and we can adjust.

Doc links/attachments: Nimbus_SOW_v1.pdf, prepay_model_20261117.xlsx and a DocuSign signature request.

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

[attachment: Nimbus_SOW_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: Anna Li <anna@nimbusanalytics.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbusanalytics.com
Date: 2026-11-30T14:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: 3-year staged prepay wallet (formal SOW attached)

Evelyn — thanks for the clear proposal and the model. Procurement is inclined to proceed but asks for two small tweaks before we sign:
1) Faster initial burn credit: can we front-load 20% of Year 1 credits for the first 90 days (we have a heavy Q1 rollout) but keep the rest on a monthly drawdown?
2) Rollover flexibility: can we increase the rollover cap to 15% for Year 1 only (we can accept 10% thereafter)?

If Redwood can accept those two adjustments we can circulate internally and route the DocuSign for signature next week.

Would like to get the redline on those items (and final SOW) by EOD Friday so procurement can complete the budget cycle.

Thanks,
Anna
Director, Cloud & ML Ops
Nimbus Analytics
